resource.name: aws_sagemaker_user_profile
resource.description: Provides a SageMaker AI User Profile resource.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of SageMaker user profiles, which serve as individual identities within a SageMaker Domain for accessing machine learning environments. It is commonly used to configure personalized settings for data scientists and ML practitioners, including resource access, permissions, and Jupyter notebook environments. This resource supports lifecycle management of user profiles, integration with IAM roles, and customization of user-specific configurations to streamline collaboration and secure access in AI/ML workflows.

examples.title: Basic usage
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates the basic setup of an AWS SageMaker User Profile by specifying the `domain_id` from an associated SageMaker Domain and defining a `user_profile_name`. This example helps users understand how to create and associate a user profile within a SageMaker Domain for managing individual user settings."

arguments.name: domain_id
arguments.description: (Required) The ID of the associated Domain.
arguments.llm_summary: The `domain_id` argument specifies the unique identifier of the SageMaker Domain to which the user profile belongs, enabling the association of the profile with a managed environment for machine learning resources and user access. By setting this required value, users define the scope and context of the user profile within the SageMaker Domain, ensuring proper integration and access control for collaborative ML workflows.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the user profile within SageMaker. While optional, setting this argument can help define a custom name or reference for the profile, enabling easier management, retrieval, and integration with other resources or workflows in the SageMaker environment.

arguments.name: single_sign_on_user_identifier
arguments.description: (Optional) A specifier for the type of value specified in `single_sign_on_user_value`. Currently, the only supported value is `UserName`. If the Domain's AuthMode is SSO, this field is required. If the Domain's AuthMode is not SSO, this field cannot be specified.
arguments.llm_summary: The `single_sign_on_user_identifier` argument allows users to specify the type of identifier (e.g., `UserName`) used to associate a SageMaker user profile with a single sign-on (SSO) user when the Domain's authentication mode is set to SSO. This configuration ensures proper linkage between the SageMaker user profile and the SSO identity, enabling seamless authentication and access management for the user.

arguments.name: single_sign_on_user_value
arguments.description: (Required) The username of the associated AWS Single Sign-On User for this User Profile. If the Domain's AuthMode is SSO, this field is required, and must match a valid username of a user in your directory. If the Domain's AuthMode is not SSO, this field cannot be specified.
arguments.llm_summary: The `single_sign_on_user_value` argument allows you to specify the username of an AWS Single Sign-On (SSO) user associated with the SageMaker User Profile. This is required when the Domain's `AuthMode` is set to SSO, enabling integration with your organization's SSO directory for user authentication and access control, but must be omitted if SSO is not used.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to assign key-value metadata to the user profile, enabling resource categorization, organization, and cost tracking. By defining tags, users can streamline management tasks such as identifying environments, applying policies, or integrating with billing and governance workflows, with provider-level default tags being overridden if matching keys are specified.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are automatically merged with resource-specific tags, enabling consistent metadata management across AWS resources. By configuring this argument, users can streamline tagging for cost allocation, access control, and resource organization, ensuring alignment with governance and operational standards.

arguments.name: user_profile_name
arguments.description: (Required) The name for the User Profile.
arguments.llm_summary: The `user_profile_name` argument specifies the unique name of the SageMaker User Profile, serving as an identifier for the profile within the SageMaker domain. By defining this required property, users can create and manage individual user environments, enabling personalized configurations and access control for machine learning workflows.

blocks.name: user_settings
blocks.description: (Required) The user settings. See User Settings below.

arguments.name: auto_mount_home_efs
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether auto-mounting of an EFS volume is supported for the user profile. The `DefaultAsDomain` value is only supported for user profiles. Do not use the `DefaultAsDomain` value when setting this parameter for a domain. Valid values are: `Enabled`, `Disabled`, and `DefaultAsDomain`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `auto_mount_home_efs` argument in the `user_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to control whether an Amazon EFS (Elastic File System) volume is automatically mounted as the home directory for the SageMaker user profile. By setting this argument to `Enabled`, `Disabled`, or `DefaultAsDomain`, users can configure storage behavior to streamline data access, manage workspace persistence, or align with domain-level defaults, supporting goals like environment setup and seamless file management for machine learning workflows.

arguments.name: default_landing_uri
arguments.description: (Optional) The default experience that the user is directed to when accessing the domain. The supported values are: `studio::`: Indicates that Studio is the default experience. This value can only be passed if StudioWebPortal is set to ENABLED. `app:JupyterServer:`: Indicates that Studio Classic is the default experience.
arguments.llm_summary: The `default_landing_uri` argument in the `user_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify the default interface or application (e.g., Studio or Studio Classic) that a SageMaker user is directed to upon accessing the domain. This configuration helps tailor the user experience by defining the initial environment based on the enabled features, such as StudioWebPortal, aligning with user workflows and preferences.

arguments.name: execution_role
arguments.description: (Required) The execution role ARN for the user.
arguments.llm_summary: The `execution_role` argument specifies the IAM role ARN that governs the permissions and access control for the SageMaker user profile's operations, ensuring the user can execute tasks like training models, accessing datasets, or interacting with other AWS services. By defining this role, users establish the security context and resource access boundaries required for the SageMaker environment to function effectively.

arguments.name: security_groups
arguments.description: (Optional) A list of security group IDs that will be attached to the user.
arguments.llm_summary: The `security_groups` argument in the `user_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify a set of security group IDs to control network access for the SageMaker user profile. By defining this argument, users can enforce specific inbound and outbound traffic rules, ensuring secure connectivity and compliance with organizational network policies for the user's SageMaker environment.

arguments.name: studio_web_portal
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether the user can access Studio. If this value is set to `DISABLED`, the user cannot access Studio, even if that is the default experience for the domain. Valid values are `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `studio_web_portal` argument in the `user_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to control whether a specific user can access the Amazon SageMaker Studio web interface. Setting this argument to `ENABLED` grants access to Studio, while `DISABLED` restricts it, overriding the domain's default experience. This configuration is typically used to manage user permissions and tailor access to SageMaker Studio based on organizational or individual requirements.

blocks.name: canvas_app_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) The Canvas app settings. See Canvas App Settings below.

blocks.name: direct_deploy_settings
blocks.description: (Optional)The model deployment settings for the SageMaker AI Canvas application. See Direct Deploy Settings below.

arguments.name: status
arguments.description: (Optional)Describes whether model deployment permissions are enabled or disabled in the Canvas application. Valid values are `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `status` argument in the `direct_deploy_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to control whether model deployment permissions are enabled or disabled in the Amazon SageMaker Canvas application. Setting this argument to `ENABLED` grants deployment capabilities, facilitating direct model deployment workflows, while `DISABLED` restricts these permissions, aligning with access control or compliance requirements.

blocks.llm_summary: The `direct_deploy_settings` block within the `canvas_app_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource configures model deployment options for the SageMaker AI Canvas application. It encapsulates settings that enable direct deployment of machine learning models, allowing users to streamline the deployment process and manage deployment-specific configurations for AI Canvas workflows.

blocks.name: emr_serverless_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) The settings for running Amazon EMR Serverless jobs in SageMaker AI Canvas. See `emr_serverless_settings` Block below.

arguments.name: execution_role_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS IAM role that is assumed for running Amazon EMR Serverless jobs in SageMaker AI Canvas. This role should have the necessary permissions to read and write data attached and a trust relationship with EMR Serverless.
arguments.llm_summary: The `execution_role_arn` argument in the `emr_serverless_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify the ARN of an IAM role that SageMaker AI Canvas assumes to execute Amazon EMR Serverless jobs. Configuring this role ensures the necessary permissions for data access and operations, enabling seamless integration and execution of serverless workflows within SageMaker.

arguments.name: status
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes whether Amazon EMR Serverless job capabilities are enabled or disabled in the SageMaker AI Canvas application. Valid values are: `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `status` argument in the `emr_serverless_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to control whether Amazon EMR Serverless job capabilities are enabled or disabled within the SageMaker AI Canvas application. By setting this argument to `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`, users can define the availability of EMR Serverless functionality, impacting the ability to run serverless data processing jobs directly from SageMaker AI Canvas.

blocks.llm_summary: The `emr_serverless_settings` block within the `canvas_app_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource configures the integration and operational parameters for running Amazon EMR Serverless jobs in SageMaker AI Canvas. This block encapsulates settings that enable users to leverage EMR Serverless for scalable, on-demand data processing and analytics workflows directly within the AI Canvas environment, facilitating seamless execution of big data tasks without managing infrastructure.

blocks.name: generative_ai_settings

arguments.name: amazon_bedrock_role_arn
arguments.llm_summary: The `amazon_bedrock_role_arn` argument in the `generative_ai_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify the ARN of an IAM role that grants permissions for accessing Amazon Bedrock services. By setting this argument, users can enable integration with generative AI capabilities provided by Amazon Bedrock, ensuring the SageMaker user profile has the necessary access to perform tasks like model inference or data processing within Bedrock.

blocks.llm_summary: The `generative_ai_settings` block within the `canvas_app_settings` configuration of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource enables and manages settings specific to generative AI capabilities in the SageMaker Canvas application. It encapsulates configurations related to the use of generative AI tools, models, or features, allowing users to customize and control access to advanced AI functionalities for data analysis and model generation. Configuring this block helps users leverage generative AI within SageMaker Canvas to enhance productivity and streamline machine learning workflows.

blocks.name: identity_provider_oauth_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) The settings for connecting to an external data source with OAuth. See Identity Provider OAuth Settings below.

arguments.name: data_source_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The name of the data source that you're connecting to. Canvas currently supports OAuth for Snowflake and Salesforce Data Cloud. Valid values are `SalesforceGenie` and `Snowflake`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `data_source_name` argument specifies the external data source (e.g., `SalesforceGenie` or `Snowflake`) to be connected via OAuth within the `identity_provider_oauth_settings` of an `aws_sagemaker_user_profile`. Configuring this argument enables seamless integration with supported data platforms, allowing users to access and utilize external datasets in SageMaker Canvas workflows.

arguments.name: secret_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of an Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager secret that stores the credentials from your identity provider, such as the client ID and secret, authorization URL, and token URL.
arguments.llm_summary: The `secret_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a Secrets Manager secret that stores OAuth credentials (e.g., client ID, client secret, authorization URL, and token URL) for the identity provider integration in SageMaker user profiles. By setting this required argument, users enable secure authentication and authorization workflows for SageMaker user profiles, ensuring seamless access control and identity federation with external identity providers.

arguments.name: status
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes whether OAuth for a data source is enabled or disabled in the Canvas application. Valid values are `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `status` argument in the `identity_provider_oauth_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify whether OAuth authentication for external data sources is enabled or disabled in the SageMaker Canvas application. By setting this argument to `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`, users can control the integration of OAuth-based identity providers, impacting the application's ability to securely access external data sources for machine learning workflows.

blocks.llm_summary: "Configures OAuth settings to enable secure integration with external identity providers for data access within the Canvas application of SageMaker. This block encapsulates authentication parameters, facilitating seamless connectivity and authorization workflows for external data sources."

blocks.name: kendra_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) The settings for document querying. See Kendra Settings below.

arguments.name: status
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes whether the document querying feature is enabled or disabled in the Canvas application. Valid values are `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `status` argument in the `kendra_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to control whether the document querying feature in the Canvas application is enabled or disabled. By setting this argument to `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`, users can define the availability of Kendra-powered search functionality, aligning the application's behavior with their data exploration and querying needs.

blocks.llm_summary: The `kendra_settings` block within the `canvas_app_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource configures the integration for document querying using Amazon Kendra. It encapsulates settings related to enabling and managing Kendra's search capabilities, allowing users to query and retrieve relevant documents within the SageMaker Canvas application, enhancing data accessibility and search efficiency.

blocks.name: model_register_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) The model registry settings for the SageMaker AI Canvas application. See Model Register Settings below.

arguments.name: cross_account_model_register_role_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SageMaker AI model registry account. Required only to register model versions created by a different SageMaker AI Canvas AWS account than the AWS account in which SageMaker AI model registry is set up.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the IAM role ARN required for cross-account model version registration in SageMaker AI model registry. This argument enables users to specify permissions for registering models created in a different AWS account, facilitating multi-account workflows and collaboration in machine learning environments.

arguments.name: status
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes whether the integration to the model registry is enabled or disabled in the Canvas application. Valid values are `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `status` argument in the `model_register_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to control whether integration with the SageMaker Model Registry is enabled or disabled within the Canvas application. By setting this argument to `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`, users can define the availability of model registry features, aligning the application’s behavior with their workflow requirements for managing and accessing registered models.

blocks.llm_summary: The `model_register_settings` block within the `canvas_app_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource configures the model registry integration for the SageMaker AI Canvas application. It enables users to manage settings related to registering, tracking, and organizing machine learning models, facilitating streamlined model lifecycle management and versioning within the AI Canvas environment.

blocks.name: time_series_forecasting_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) Time series forecast settings for the Canvas app. See Time Series Forecasting Settings below.

arguments.name: amazon_forecast_role_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The IAM role that Canvas passes to Amazon Forecast for time series forecasting. By default, Canvas uses the execution role specified in the UserProfile that launches the Canvas app. If an execution role is not specified in the UserProfile, Canvas uses the execution role specified in the Domain that owns the UserProfile. To allow time series forecasting, this IAM role should have the AmazonSageMakerCanvasForecastAccess policy attached and forecast.amazonaws.com added in the trust relationship as a service principal.
arguments.llm_summary: The `amazon_forecast_role_arn` argument in the `time_series_forecasting_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify an IAM role that grants Amazon SageMaker Canvas the necessary permissions to interact with Amazon Forecast for time series forecasting tasks. Configuring this role enables Canvas to perform forecasting operations by ensuring the role has the required `AmazonSageMakerCanvasForecastAccess` policy and trust relationship with `forecast.amazonaws.com`.

arguments.name: status
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes whether time series forecasting is enabled or disabled in the Canvas app. Valid values are `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `status` argument in the `time_series_forecasting_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to control whether time series forecasting functionality is enabled or disabled in the SageMaker Canvas application. By setting this argument to `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`, users can define the availability of forecasting features, aligning the application's behavior with their data analysis and modeling requirements.

blocks.llm_summary: "Configures time series forecasting capabilities within the Canvas app for the SageMaker user profile, enabling users to define settings that optimize and manage forecasting workflows. This block allows for fine-tuned control over forecasting features, supporting advanced analytics and predictive modeling use cases."

blocks.name: workspace_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) The workspace settings for the SageMaker AI Canvas application. See Workspace Settings below.

arguments.name: s3_artifact_path
arguments.description: (Optional) The Amazon S3 bucket used to store artifacts generated by Canvas. Updating the Amazon S3 location impacts existing configuration settings, and Canvas users no longer have access to their artifacts. Canvas users must log out and log back in to apply the new location.
arguments.llm_summary: The `s3_artifact_path` argument in the `workspace_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify the Amazon S3 bucket location for storing artifacts generated by SageMaker Canvas. Configuring this path enables control over artifact storage but impacts existing configurations, requiring Canvas users to log out and back in to access the updated location, aligning with goals like managing data storage and ensuring proper artifact accessibility.

arguments.name: s3_kms_key_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The Amazon Web Services Key Management Service (KMS) encryption key ID that is used to encrypt artifacts generated by Canvas in the Amazon S3 bucket.
arguments.llm_summary: The `s3_kms_key_id` argument in the `workspace_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify the AWS KMS encryption key ID for securing artifacts generated by SageMaker Canvas in an associated S3 bucket. By configuring this argument, users can enforce data encryption at rest, aligning with security and compliance requirements for sensitive data storage.

blocks.llm_summary: The `workspace_settings` block within the `canvas_app_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource defines configuration options for the SageMaker AI Canvas workspace environment. It encapsulates settings that manage the operational behavior and customization of the workspace, enabling users to tailor the AI Canvas application to their specific data science and machine learning workflows. Configuring this block allows for precise control over workspace functionality, ensuring an optimized and user-specific experience for AI and data visualization tasks.

"Configures settings for the SageMaker Canvas application within the `user_settings` of an `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource, enabling control over user access and functionality for low-code/no-code machine learning workflows. This block encapsulates options related to the Canvas app environment, allowing users to tailor the experience and permissions for streamlined data exploration and model creation."

blocks.name: code_editor_app_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) The Code Editor application settings. See Code Editor App Settings below.

arguments.name: built_in_lifecycle_config_arn
arguments.llm_summary: The `built_in_lifecycle_config_arn` argument allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a predefined lifecycle configuration for the code editor application within the SageMaker user profile. By setting this argument, users can control the initialization and shutdown behavior of the code editor environment, such as preloading specific configurations, automating resource cleanup, or defining environment setup tasks, aligning with common goals like streamlining development workflows and enforcing consistency across user sessions.

arguments.name: lifecycle_config_arns
arguments.description: (Optional) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lifecycle Configurations.
arguments.llm_summary: The `lifecycle_config_arns` argument in the `code_editor_app_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify a set of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) for Lifecycle Configurations that define custom initialization and teardown scripts for the SageMaker Studio code editor environment. By setting this argument, users can automate environment setup, manage resource cleanup, and enforce consistent configurations, aligning with common goals like environment standardization and operational efficiency.

blocks.name: app_lifecycle_management
idle_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) Settings related to idle shutdown of Studio applications. see `idle_settings` Block below.

arguments.name: idle_timeout_in_minutes
arguments.description: (Optional) The time that SageMaker AI waits after the application becomes idle before shutting it down. Valid values are between `60` and `525600`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `idle_timeout_in_minutes` argument for the `idle_settings` block in the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to define the duration (in minutes) that SageMaker waits before automatically shutting down an idle application. This configuration helps optimize resource usage and cost by controlling the application's lifecycle based on inactivity, with valid values ranging from 60 minutes to 525,600 minutes.

arguments.name: lifecycle_management
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether idle shutdown is activated for the application type. Valid values are `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `lifecycle_management` argument in the `idle_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to control whether idle shutdown is activated for the associated application type. By specifying `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`, users can define the application's behavior for managing idle resources, helping optimize cost and resource utilization by automatically shutting down inactive sessions.

arguments.name: max_idle_timeout_in_minutes
arguments.description: (Optional) The maximum value in minutes that custom idle shutdown can be set to by the user. Valid values are between `60` and `525600`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_idle_timeout_in_minutes` argument for the `idle_settings` in the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to define the maximum duration (in minutes) that a custom idle shutdown can be configured for SageMaker user sessions. By setting this value, users can control resource optimization and cost management by limiting idle time before automatic shutdown, with valid values ranging from 60 minutes to 525,600 minutes (1 year).

arguments.name: min_idle_timeout_in_minutes
arguments.description: (Optional) The minimum value in minutes that custom idle shutdown can be set to by the user. Valid values are between `60` and `525600`.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the minimum allowable idle timeout, in minutes, that users can configure for automatic shutdown of SageMaker resources, ensuring control over resource utilization and cost management. This setting enforces a lower limit within the range of `60` to `525600` minutes, aligning with operational policies or usage constraints.

blocks.llm_summary: The `idle_settings` block in the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource under "app_lifecycle_management" configures parameters for automatically shutting down idle Studio applications, optimizing resource usage and cost management. It encapsulates settings related to idle timeout behavior, enabling users to enforce lifecycle policies that prevent unnecessary resource consumption during periods of inactivity.

The `app_lifecycle_management` block within the `code_editor_app_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource configures lifecycle management settings for applications in the SageMaker code editor environment. It enables users to define and control the behavior of application initialization, updates, and termination, facilitating streamlined management of app states and ensuring consistent development workflows.

blocks.name: custom_image
blocks.description: (Optional) A list of custom SageMaker AI images that are configured to run as a CodeEditor app. see Custom Image below.

arguments.name: app_image_config_name

arguments.llm_summary: The `app_image_config_name` argument specifies the name of the App Image Config associated with a custom image in the SageMaker user profile. This configuration defines runtime settings such as environment variables, kernel specifications, or file system mounts for the custom image, enabling users to tailor the execution environment for their machine learning workflows.

arguments.name: image_name
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the Custom Image.
arguments.llm_summary: The `image_name` argument specifies the unique name of the Custom Image associated with the SageMaker user profile, enabling users to define the specific container image used for their development environment or workflows. By setting this required property, users can customize the runtime environment to include pre-configured tools, libraries, or dependencies tailored to their machine learning tasks.

arguments.name: image_version_number
arguments.description: (Optional) The version number of the Custom Image.
arguments.llm_summary: The `image_version_number` argument allows users to specify the version of a custom image associated with the SageMaker user profile, enabling precise control over the image's configuration and ensuring compatibility with specific development or runtime environments. By setting this argument, users can manage versioning to align with their workflows, such as deploying updates or maintaining consistency across machine learning projects.

blocks.llm_summary: The `custom_image` block within the `code_editor_app_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource defines a list of custom SageMaker AI images tailored for use in the CodeEditor application. This configuration enables users to specify pre-built or custom container images that provide a controlled development environment, facilitating customization of tools, libraries, and runtime settings for AI/ML workflows in SageMaker.

blocks.name: default_resource_spec
blocks.description: (Optional) The default instance type and the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the SageMaker AI image created on the instance. see Default Resource Spec below.

arguments.name: instance_type
arguments.description: (Optional) The instance type that the image version runs on.. For valid values see SageMaker AI Instance Types.
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_type` argument in the `default_resource_spec` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify the compute instance type on which the associated image version will run. Configuring this argument enables users to tailor the computational capacity and performance of the SageMaker environment to match their workload requirements, such as training models or running data processing tasks, by selecting from valid SageMaker AI instance types.

arguments.name: lifecycle_config_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lifecycle Configuration attached to the Resource.
arguments.llm_summary: Specifies the ARN of a SageMaker Lifecycle Configuration to attach to the user profile's default resource, enabling the automation of custom setup or teardown scripts for the associated compute environments. This allows users to define and manage environment initialization tasks, such as installing dependencies or configuring settings, to streamline and standardize resource behavior.

arguments.name: sagemaker_image_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the SageMaker AI image that the image version belongs to.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sagemaker_image_arn` argument in the `default_resource_spec` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a SageMaker AI image associated with the image version. By setting this argument, users can define the underlying container image used for the user's default compute environment, enabling customization of the tools, libraries, and runtime for machine learning workflows within SageMaker Studio.

arguments.name: sagemaker_image_version_alias
arguments.description: (Optional) The SageMaker AI Image Version Alias.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sagemaker_image_version_alias` argument allows users to specify an alias for a specific version of a SageMaker AI image within the `default_resource_spec` configuration of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource. By setting this alias, users can streamline image version management, enabling consistent references to specific image versions for training or inference environments, which supports reproducibility and simplifies updates across SageMaker workflows.

arguments.name: sagemaker_image_version_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN of the image version created on the instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `sagemaker_image_version_arn` argument allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a specific SageMaker image version to be used in the `default_resource_spec` configuration for the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource. By setting this argument, users can control the runtime environment for SageMaker instances associated with the user profile, enabling customization of pre-configured software, libraries, and dependencies for machine learning workflows.

blocks.llm_summary: "Defines the default compute instance type and SageMaker AI image ARN for the code editor application within the user profile, enabling streamlined configuration of the development environment's underlying resources. This block ensures consistent and optimized resource allocation for AI-driven code editing workflows."

"Defines configuration for the Code Editor application within SageMaker user profiles, enabling customization of editor-specific settings under 'user_settings.' blocks.name: custom_file_system_config
blocks.description: (Optional) The settings for assigning a custom file system to a user profile. Permitted users can access this file system in Amazon SageMaker AI Studio. See Custom File System Config below.

arguments.name: file_system_id
arguments.description: (Required) The ID of your Amazon EFS file system.
arguments.llm_summary: The `file_system_id` argument specifies the unique identifier of an Amazon EFS file system to be mounted and used within the `efs_file_system_config` of an `aws_sagemaker_user_profile`. By defining this ID, users enable seamless integration of persistent, shared storage for SageMaker user profiles, supporting workflows that require durable and scalable file storage for data access and collaboration.

arguments.name: file_system_path
arguments.description: (Required) The path to the file system directory that is accessible in Amazon SageMaker AI Studio. Permitted users can access only this directory and below.
arguments.llm_summary: The `file_system_path` argument in the `efs_file_system_config` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to specify the directory path within an Amazon EFS file system that is accessible to SageMaker AI Studio users. By setting this argument, users can control the scope of file system access, ensuring that permitted users can interact only with the defined directory and its subdirectories, supporting secure and organized data management for machine learning workflows.

blocks.llm_summary: The `efs_file_system_config` block within the `custom_file_system_config` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource defines the default settings for integrating an Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) with a SageMaker user profile's private space. It encapsulates configuration details for EFS storage, enabling persistent, scalable, and shared file system access for data and artifacts in SageMaker environments, helping users manage storage for collaborative machine learning workflows.

"Defines settings to integrate a custom file system with a SageMaker user profile, enabling users to access and utilize the file system within Amazon SageMaker Studio. This block configures file system parameters to support custom storage needs for data and workflows in AI/ML development environments."

blocks.name: custom_posix_user_config
blocks.description: (Optional) Details about the POSIX identity that is used for file system operations. See Custom Posix User Config below.

arguments.name: gid
arguments.description: (Optional) The POSIX group ID.
arguments.llm_summary: The `gid` argument in the `custom_posix_user_config` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource specifies the POSIX group ID (GID) for the SageMaker user profile, ensuring the user is associated with a specific group in a POSIX-compliant file system. This configuration is essential for managing file permissions, access control, and collaboration within SageMaker environments that rely on POSIX-based systems.

arguments.name: uid
arguments.description: (Optional) The POSIX user ID.
arguments.llm_summary: The `uid` argument in the `custom_posix_user_config` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to define the POSIX user ID (UID) for the SageMaker user profile, ensuring compatibility with POSIX-compliant systems and enabling precise identity mapping for file and resource access. By setting this required numeric value, users can control how the SageMaker user interacts with underlying file systems and processes, aligning with security, access control, and system integration requirements.

blocks.llm_summary: The `custom_posix_user_config` block within the `user_settings` of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource defines POSIX identity settings for file system operations, enabling precise control over user and group IDs for managing file access and permissions. By setting this argument, users can automate environment setup tasks, enforce consistent configurations, or implement cleanup processes, aligning with common goals like streamlining workspace management and ensuring reproducibility in SageMaker workflows.

blocks.name: app_lifecycle_management
blocks.description: (Optional) Indicates whether idle shutdown is activated for JupyterLab applications. see `app_lifecycle_management` Block below.

blocks.name: idle_settings
blocks.description: (Optional) Settings related to idle shutdown of Studio applications. see `idle_settings` Block below.

arguments.name: idle_timeout_in_minutes
arguments.description: (Optional) The time that SageMaker AI waits after the application becomes idle before shutting it down. Valid values are between `60` and `525600`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `idle_timeout_in_minutes` argument for the `idle_settings` block in the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to define the duration (in minutes) that SageMaker waits before automatically shutting down an idle application. This configuration helps optimize resource usage and cost by controlling the application's lifecycle based on inactivity, with valid values ranging from 60 minutes to 525,600 minutes.

arguments.name: lifecycle_management
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether idle shutdown is activated for the application type. Valid values are `ENABLED` and `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `lifecycle_management` argument in the `idle_settings` block of the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to control whether idle shutdown is activated for the associated application type. By setting this argument to `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`, users can define the application's behavior for managing idle resources, helping optimize cost and resource utilization by automatically shutting down inactive sessions.

arguments.name: max_idle_timeout_in_minutes
arguments.description: (Optional) The maximum value in minutes that custom idle shutdown can be set to by the user. Valid values are between `60` and `525600`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_idle_timeout_in_minutes` argument for the `idle_settings` in the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource allows users to define the maximum duration (in minutes) that a custom idle shutdown can be configured for SageMaker user sessions. By setting this value, users can control resource optimization and cost management by limiting idle time, with valid values ranging from 60 minutes to 525,600 minutes (1 year).

arguments.name: min_idle_timeout_in_minutes
arguments.description: (Optional) The minimum value in minutes that custom idle shutdown can be set to by the user. Valid values are between `60` and `525600`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `min_idle_timeout_in_minutes` argument for the `idle_settings` in the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource defines the minimum allowable duration (in minutes) for custom idle shutdown settings, ensuring that users can specify idle timeout thresholds within a valid range of 60 to 525,600 minutes. This configuration helps control resource utilization and cost efficiency by enforcing limits on idle session durations in SageMaker environments.

blocks.llm_summary: The `idle_settings` block in the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource under "app_lifecycle_management" configures parameters for automatically shutting down idle Studio applications, optimizing resource usage and cost management. It encapsulates settings related to idle timeout behavior, enabling users to enforce lifecycle policies that prevent unnecessary resource consumption during periods of inactivity.

The `app_lifecycle_management` block within `jupyter_lab_app_settings` for the `aws_sagemaker_user_profile` resource enables control over the lifecycle behavior of JupyterLab applications, specifically managing idle shutdown settings to optimize resource usage. Configuring this block allows users to automate application shutdown during inactivity, ensuring efficient resource management and cost savings in SageMaker environments.
